key_insight: Trigonal selenium appears intrinsically defect tolerant: even though many point defects create deep gap states, their SRH recombination is strongly suppressed by large lattice reorganization and large energy release.
engineering_relevance: This makes t-Se a promising wide-band-gap absorber for tandem and indoor photovoltaics, where defect tolerance can reduce performance penalties from unavoidable material imperfections.
method: First-principles calculations of a large, chemically diverse set of point defects in trigonal selenium.
Quantified defect-assisted Shockley-Read-Hall recombination, including radiative capture and nonradiative multi-phonon emission.
Analyzed trends versus defect level position, lattice relaxation, charge state, and doping conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that realistic concentrations of point defects cannot explain the observed efficiency losses, with nonradiative recombination suppressed by energy releases of at least 0.5 Eg per event.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on idealized first-principles defect modeling, so real-device losses from extended defects, interfaces, or extrinsic impurities may still matter.
paper_title: Defect Tolerance in Trigonal Selenium Photovoltaics
